title: Encore Theater
paragraphs: A 1946 dramatic anthology based on true stories from medicine, including doctors, patients, research breakthroughs, and the personal costs of medical work.
Thirteen-program CBS summer dramatic anthology built around medicine, medical history, doctors, researchers and patients.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS/Schenley summer run (June 4, 1946 to August 27, 1946) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Frank Graham (announcer), Jean Holloway (radio adaptor and writer), Bill Lawrence (director and producer), Leith Stevens (conductor, music, and composer), [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer), Norman Field (performer), and Earle Ross (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].

The stories often return to illness, patients and recovery, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, medicine and medical practice, medical ethics, duty and sacrifice, medical-themed literary and film adaptation, and medical biography and history.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar American medical and scientific interest, CBS 1946 summer replacement season, Schenley Laboratories sponsorship, and Complete surviving thirteen-program run.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], and [[show|the-halls-of-ivy|The Halls of Ivy]].
